clue.text: Tax point in addition covers large hotel

indicators.note: covers says the phrase for 'in addition' wraps round the letter for large

parts.note: 'to boot' is an idiom meaning in addition
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tax bill for a big hotel with extra charges piled on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' is an idiom for in addition; 'covers' signals the enclosure of L.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a booth or town hall where tolls and dues were collected, so a place where tax was paid.

clue.text: Women's record time greeted effusively

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A women's world-record time is met with gushing applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' is Scots for weep or cry, so 'greeted effusively' means cried copiously; the surface suggests welcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect to greet is to cry, so to have greeted with plenty of tears is to have shed them freely.

clue.text: Senseless state positions retreating troops

indicators.note: retreating says the word for positions goes backwards

parts.note: to position something is to put it, so positions = puts
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A dazed army as soldiers fall back from their positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' applies only to the positions word; OR (other ranks) is a standard term for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A daze in which one is barely conscious is a state without feeling or awareness.

clue.text: Skinflint goes crazy munching odd bits of carrot

indicators.note: munching says the jumbled letters take in and enclose the picked letters
crazy signals that the letters of goes are jumbled
odd bits means the first, third and fifth letters of carrot

explanation.surface: A miser loses his mind while eating scraps of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles the four letters of goes; 'munching' has them swallow the odd letters of carrot after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Ebenezer of A Christmas Carol is so famously mean that his surname is a byword for a miser.

clue.text: Love is thwarted in books one writes

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the books abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: thwarted signals the letters of 'love is' are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A tale of frustrated romance found between the covers of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thwarted' scrambles 'love is'; 'in' sets the result inside the New Testament abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiction author is someone who writes long prose stories.

clue.text: Left writer fitting in second episode

indicators.note: fitting in says the two short pieces are slotted inside the word for second

parts.note: a second or an instant is a very short moment
the writer of the clue refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A left-wing author slots into a second episode of a serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left writer' looks like a political author; 'writer' is the setter speaking of himself. 'fitting in' places both inside the word for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's novels came out in parts, each part of a serial being one episode.

clue.text: Yellow and black bird caught first

indicators.note: first says the letter for caught comes before the bird

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a raven is a large black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A yellow and black bird is captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' looks like a colour beside black; it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being yellow is slang for being a coward, and craven means cowardly.

clue.text: Household Words?

definitions.meaning: having words means arguing, and a ... is a row between people who live together

explanation.surface: Household Words was the title of a weekly magazine that Dickens edited.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of the home; as a noun it is a quarrel at home, which is having words.

clue.text: Haver, beginning to abandon drug

indicators.note: beginning to abandon tells us the drug word loses its first letter

parts.note: a downer is a depressant drug

explanation.surface: Someone dithering as they start to give up drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haver' (one who dithers in Scots) misleads; read it as one who has.
explanation.definitionFit: A haver is one who has something, which is a possessor or proprietor.

clue.text: Go round denying Republican's remarks on passing

indicators.note: denying says the Republican is refused entry, so its letter is taken out

parts.note: to orbit is to go round

explanation.surface: Someone goes round refusing a Republican's comments made in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarks on passing' sounds casual, but passing here is death.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a notice written about someone who has died.

clue.text: Screening show about sleuth Italian's backing

indicators.note: about puts the word for show round the detective and Italian pieces

parts.note: to prove something is to show it
TEC is short for detective, a sleuth

indicators.note: backing says the Italian abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: A TV show about an Italian detective's supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses only the Italian abbreviation; 'about' wraps the show word round both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to shelter it, so screening is shielding or guarding.

clue.text: Dickens protagonist rebuffs field officer

indicators.note: rebuffs says the hero's name rejects and drops the word field

parts.note: David Copperfield is the hero of Dickens's novel of that name

explanation.surface: A Dickens hero snubs a senior army officer in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'field officer' reads as a military rank; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: A copper is British slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Irrational old man conducted test involving medium

parts.note: PA is a familiar word for father, one's old man
to run a business is to conduct it, so conducted = ran

indicators.note: involving says the test word contains the letter for medium

parts.note: an oral is a spoken test or exam
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: An irrational father holds a seance testing a medium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' sits in the seance scene but just gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond normal scientific explanation, so not to be accounted for by reason.

clue.text: Good call about hostile interrogation

indicators.note: about places the phone-call word round the word for hostile

parts.note: to give someone a ring is to call them
ill as in ill will means hostile

explanation.surface: A sensible phone call about a hostile questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: A long and searching questioning, as by police, is called a severe quizzing.

clue.text: Prince Charming wants china the French added

indicators.note: added says the French article joins on at the end
wants means lacks, so the china word is removed

parts.note: Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: Prince Charming of the pantomime needs porcelain with French flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince Charming' reads as one name; 'Prince' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The then heir to the throne bore this name, so he is a prince known by it.

clue.text: Finish importing European energy, working in hardship

indicators.note: importing says the finish word takes in the other two pieces

parts.note: an end is a finish
a Slav is a European from a Slavic people
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Eurozone energy deal falls through, leaving workers in hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' has the finish word take in the European and energy pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in slavery is made to toil under harsh conditions.

clue.text: Scatter most of the crumbs

parts.note: to strew is to scatter

indicators.note: most of says the last letter of the word the is dropped

explanation.surface: Scatter nearly all the breadcrumbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbs' looks like bread; it is the mild exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, crumbs British and the other Australian-flavoured slang.

clue.text: Topical article, dull in character primarily

parts.note: the is the definite article
mat, or matt, means dull, not glossy

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on current events that is dull in nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a topic or subject, so concerned with themes.

clue.text: Coach first of all drives all over the place

indicators.note: first of means take the opening letter of all
all over the place signals the letters of drives are scattered

explanation.surface: A coach driver who careers all over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus; it is a trainer. 'all over the place' makes DVISER from DRIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach gives instruction and guidance, so is a counsellor.

clue.text: Worried sea dog in rocks

indicators.note: rocks signals the letters are shaken about

explanation.surface: An old sailor is anxious about being on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to worry intensely, so this is the past participle for fretting.

clue.text: 4's visitors make grand MCs

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
masters of ceremonies host shows, so MCs = hosts

explanation.surface: Masters of ceremonies earning a thousand each.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 down is the miser of A Christmas Carol, who is visited by spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits of Christmas past, present and future call on the miser of 4 down.

clue.text: Latvian ruler's character

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A Latvian monarch's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like personality; it is a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written symbol such as one of the alphabet's.

clue.text: Short story about dry lake

indicators.note: about places the story word round the other pieces

parts.note: a story can be a lie or fib
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry

explanation.surface: A brief tale about a lake that has dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short story' reads as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Short in size or amount is small.

clue.text: Hack majority of trip with top celebs

indicators.note: majority of says most of the trip word is kept, its tail dropped

parts.note: a journey is a trip
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A hack hitches a ride on most of a trip with A-list stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' drops EY from JOURNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack is a disparaging name for a newspaper writer.

clue.text: Lacklustre Eisteddfod winner retired

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the winner's title is read backwards

parts.note: at the Welsh Eisteddfod festival the chief poetry prize goes to a bard

explanation.surface: A dull Welsh festival champion who has stepped down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of poetry and music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacklustre means dull and colourless, without brightness.

clue.text: It's run up by girl coming out close to midnight

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a girl coming out into society

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of midnight

explanation.surface: A debutante racks up bills until nearly midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' is the debutante's launch into society.
explanation.definitionFit: One runs up an amount owed, as on a credit card, so this is what is run up.

clue.text: Deal from cedar trees brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words cedar trees

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deal involving cedar trees being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' finds EDART across the two words; 'brought back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is commerce, buying and selling, so a deal is a piece of it.

clue.text: Old liberal teacher withdraws evidence of Book 9

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: withdraws says the teacher word pulls back, read in reverse

parts.note: sir is a schoolboy's name for a male teacher

explanation.surface: An elderly liberal-minded schoolmaster retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is OWNER, so the definition is evidence of a book's owner: the Latin label in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookplate marked 'from the books of' a person shows who possesses the volume.
